Nature Communications: Dynamism and evolvability in nucleic acid enzymes
item.description: Dynamism and evolvability link enzyme flexibility to adaptive potential, yet how these concepts apply to nucleic acid enzymes is largely unexplored. Here the authors compare the evolution of threose nucleic acids (TNA) and DNA-based enzymes, and show the rigid TNA backbone limits adaptability.

item.title: Nature Communications: Epigenetic repression of IL-1β by C1QBP restricts Dectin-1-mediated host defense against murine invasive candidiasis
item.description: Engagement of Dectin-1 on dendritic cells drives IL-1β production and is a critical component of the immune response to invasive candidiasis. Here the authors show epigenetic repression of IL-1β by a complement binding protein can restrain the dectin1 driven immune response in a murine model of invasive candidiasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: TogoPhosTAC as a delivery-ready platform for targeted protein dephosphorylation
item.description: This study presents togoPhosTAC, a biologic platform that directs engineered phosphatases to target proteins for phosphate removal, reducing pathological tau phosphorylation and alleviating behavioral deficits in male PS19 tauopathy mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: USP5 acts as a proteolytic switch to control SDE2 function via UBL-directed cleavage
item.description: Deubiquitinases (DUBs) are canonically defined by their ability to process ubiquitin, but this may represent only part of their biological function. Here, the authors identify USP5 as the protease that cleaves SDE2, revealing an unexpected non-canonical activity of DUBs in RNA splicing regulation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Weakly supervised artificial intelligence for multi-cancer detection of lymph node metastasis on whole slide images
item.description: The identification of lymph node metastasis remains time-consuming and error-prone for pathologists. Here, the authors develop MambaMIL+HiLA-MIL, a multiple instance learning model that allows the accurate detection of lymph node metastasis, particularly isolated tumor cells and micro-metastasis across multi-cancer and various individual cancer types from histopathology images.

item.title: Nature Communications: Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning
item.description: Here, the authors introduce deep receptor scanning methodology to enable characterization of 940 human GPCRs in parallel. This approach can be coupled to a variety of assays to systematically profile the activity and pharmacology of nearly all human GPCRs.

item.title: Nature Communications: DHODH inhibition drives albumin-mediated drug resistance through TERF2IP lactylation-activated macropinosome-mitochondria contact
item.description: DHODH inhibition triggers TERF2IP lactylation, unmasking its moonlighting transcription of epiregulin to drive EGFR-dependent macropinocytosis; macropinosome–mitochondria contact routes albumin onto DHODH, a resistance axis reversed by EGFR blockade.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cell Painting in activated cells illuminates phenotypic dark space and drug mechanisms of action
item.description: In this work, researchers show that activating cells before imaging reveals drug effects undetected under standard conditions, identifying unreported phenotypes for hundreds of compounds and identifying a natural product as a glucocorticoid receptor modulator.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural insights into Sld3-Sld7-dependent Cdc45 loading during replication initiation
item.description: DNA replication depends on loading Cdc45 onto the MCM2-7 helicase to start DNA unwinding. Here, the authors use cryo-EM to show how phosphorylation enables Sld3-Sld7 to bind MCM2-7 and position Cdc45 for helicase activation.

item.title: Nature Communications: A permeable protein nanocage enables facile cargo loading and cytosolic protein delivery
item.description: Cytosolic delivery of therapeutic proteins remains a challenge in drug delivery. Here, the authors report the discovery and characterisation of a permeable encapsulin based protein nanocage and use it to develop a modular nanocarrier for cytosolic protein delivery.

item.title: Nature Communications: A regulator of amino acid catabolism controls Acinetobacter baumannii gut colonization
item.description: Asymptomatic gut colonization is a reservoir for antimicrobial resistance (AMR) such as by the bacterium Acinetobacter baumannii . Geary and Ren, et al ., report that A. baumannii evolved a regulator that helps sense competition from the gut microbiota.

item.title: Nature Communications: Determinants of functional burden pleiotropy and gene dosage responses across human traits
item.description: Gene dosage can help explain comorbidities in developmental pediatric and psychiatric disorders. Here, the authors map how rare copy-number variants disrupting tissue and cell-type gene sets shape 43 human traits.

item.title: Nature Communications: Eradication of MRSA biofilm-associated implant infections by low-immunogenic sustained-release lysostaphin fused to thermosensitive polypeptides
item.description: Authors present an antimicrobial characterisation of their elastin-like polypeptide-fused lysostaphin, which offers enhanced stability, low immunogenicity and sustained release via injection. It safely and completely eradicates in vivo MRSA biofilm infections, outperforming lysostaphin and vancomycin.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evolutionary conservation analysis reveals a primordial function of STING as a regulator of lipid metabolism via FADS2
item.description: STING is a well-known activator of type I interferon (IFN-I) responses. However, it is debated whether STING has an ancestral function independent of interferon responses. Here, by combining evolutionary comparative analysis and lipidomics, the authors show that STING homologs regulate polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) metabolism via FADS2 and that this primordial STING-mediated metabolic control regulates responses to viral infections independently of antiviral IFN-I signaling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Enhancing iNKT cell immunotherapy through the integration of optimized CAR endodomains and iNKT engagers
item.description: iNKT cells are a subset of T cells with both innate and adaptive features, emerging as a promising immunotherapy platform due to their rapid response. Here, the authors develop a CAR-iNKT strategy incorporating a CD28ζ co-stimulatory domain and two bispecific iNKT engagers to enhance multiple myeloma targeting.

item.title: Nature Communications: Unraveling the coastal marine plastisphere archaeome
item.description: Plastic pollution creates new habitats for microbes in the ocean, but little is known about how it affects archaea. Here, the authors characterized the plastisphere archaeome and the associated potential ecological impacts from bulk water samples paired with microplastics.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bio-inspired decision making in robot swarms under biases
item.description: thanks Motoaki Hiraga, and the other, anonymous, reviewers for their contribution to the peer review of this work.

item.title: Nature Communications: Endothelial cell-microglia crosstalk mediates heart failure-associated synaptic loss and cognitive impairment in male mice
item.description: Cardiac failure is associated with cognitive impairment. Here, the authors show that blood-borne signals can induce brain endothelial cell-release of SPARC, resulting in the activation of microglia, synapse loss, and cognitive decline following transverse aortic constriction in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Deciphering the evolutionary origin of the enantioselectivity of short-chain dehydrogenases from plants toward 1-borneol
item.description: Enzyme engineering has enabled optimization of enzymes for biotechnological processes, however, less is known about how natural evolution creates new functionalities. Here, the authors investigate the evolutionary emergence of enantioselectivity in plant borneol dehydrogenases using ancestral sequence reconstruction, structural analysis, site-directed mutagenesis and computational simulations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Safety and immunogenicity of inactivated human Rotavirus vaccine in young children and infants: a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, phase I clinical trial
item.description: This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, dose escalation phase I trial evaluates the safety and immunogenicity of an inactivated rotavirus vaccine (IRV) in healthy young children and infants without prior rotavirus vaccination or HIV infection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Complementary and opponent value signals in the human brain support choosing the best and avoiding the worst
item.description: Intracranial recordings reveal complementary and opponent value signals in ventromedial prefrontal cortex and anterior insula that encode pleasant and unpleasant value and guide human choice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Column switching liquid chromatography dual mass spectrometry system for simultaneous untargeted metabolomics and targeted exposomics
item.description: Exposome-wide association studies require measuring many metabolites and environmental chemicals in the same samples. Here, the authors develop a column-switching dual-mass-spectrometry method that profiles metabolites and quantifies 601 chemical exposures in one injection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tubular ACSM3 controls fatty acid metabolism and safeguards against acute kidney injury in male mice
item.description: Fatty acid oxidation impairment represents a hallmark of acute kidney injury (AKI). Here the authors report that tubular deficiency of ACSM3, an enzyme involved in medium chain fatty acid activation, is protective against kidney injury in male mouse models of AKI potentially via modulating PPARα activity.

item.title: Nature Communications: A single computational objective can produce specialization of streams in visual cortex
item.description: Visual streams are often explained as pathways optimized for different behaviors. Here, the authors show that brain-like stream organization can instead arise from a single self-supervised objective under local spatial constraints.

item.title: Nature Communications: Stepwise allelic trajectory of ETP2 underlies trade-off between UVB tolerance and submergence adaptation in Arabidopsis thaliana
item.description: Here, the authors show that a WRKY36-ETP2-EIN2/WRKY22 module balances UVB and flood tolerance in Arabidopsis. They identify a promoter deletion in a Tibet accession that boosts UVB defense but reduces flood tolerance, while a SNP fine-tunes repression, suggesting stepwise climate adaptation.

item.title: Nature Communications: InsP3R signaling and actomyosin-dependent mitochondrial dynamics play essential roles in mitochondrial stress-induced longevity
item.description: Mitochondrial perturbations confer longevity or disease depending on if cells successfully adapt. Here, the authors show that ER calcium signalling promotes longevity during mitochondrial stress by regulating actin-dependent mitochondrial remodeling.

item.title: Nature Communications: MuSpAn: a toolbox for multiscale spatial analysis
item.description: Bull, Moore, and colleagues present MuSpAn, a flexible platform for analysing spatial biology data across scales. It integrates diverse methods to enable quantitative characterisation of tissue organisation and reveals coordinated fibroblast-immune interactions in colorectal cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-component self-assembling protein nanoparticles displaying stabilized prefusion-closed hemagglutinin trimers for influenza vaccine development
item.description: In this study, the authors rationally engineered stabilized HA trimers and HA-presenting self-assembling protein nanoparticles and show that they induce robust immune responses and confer protection in mice, supporting structure-guided development of next-generation influenza vaccines.

item.title: Nature Communications: The metabolic and anatomical complexity of root microhabitats modulate their interaction with the microbiota
item.description: In Lemnaceae , inherent root anatomy complexity determines microbiota-driven plasticity, enhancing survival in competitive environments. This plasticity links to metabolic reprogramming and is regulated by the metabolite N 6 ,N 6 ,N 6 -Trimethyl-L-lysine.

item.title: Nature Communications: A glycolytic intermediate gatekeeps global mRNA decay in Escherichia coli
item.description: RNA degradation is linked to cellular metabolism, but the underlying mechanisms are not fully understood. Here, the authors show that the glycolytic metabolite fructose 1,6‑bisphosphate inhibits PNPase activity, connecting metabolic state to RNA stability and post‑transcriptional gene regulation in bacteria.

item.title: Nature Communications: pH-Sensitive Amino Lipid-Driven Pore Formation Enables Endosomal Escape of Lipid Nanoparticles
item.description: Lipid nanoparticles have transformed nanomedicine, but the mechanisms are not fully understood. Here, the authors use molecular simulations and reveal a stalk– pore pathway for lipid nanoparticle fusion with endosomal membranes and nucleic acid release, identifying pH sensitivity, lipid transfer, shape, tension and cargo as key controls of escape.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural determinants for FAT10 activation and transfer from UBA6 to E2 enzymes
item.description: Cryo-EM captures FAT10 activation and transfer from UBA6 to E2 UBE2Z, revealing FAT10 monopolises UBA6. Efficient transfer requires E2 engagement of both FAT10 UBL domains, particularly UBL2, and co-ordination of InsP₆ in the UBA6 catalytic domain.

item.title: Nature Communications: Inhibition of RhoA-mediated secretory autophagy in megakaryocytes mitigates myelofibrosis in mice
item.description: In this study, Becker et al. demonstrate that bone marrow-resident megakaryocytes release profibrotic cytokines such as TGFβ1 via RhoA-mediated secretory autophagy. Targeting this process in vivo alleviates fibrosis progression in a preclinical mouse model of myelofibrosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis of fatty acid activation and transport by human FATP2
item.description: Here, the high resolution cryo-EM structures of human FATP2 in both the pre-catalytic and intermediate states, combined with biochemical validations, reveal a catalysis-dependent mechanism for FATP2-mediated fatty acid transport.

item.title: Nature Communications: The transmission-blocking dynamics of Plasmodium falciparum sexual-stage antibody responses in a six-year cohort of Ugandan children and adults
item.description: The study found that naturally acquired immunity that reduces malaria transmission was rare but persistent in a minority of individuals. Transmission reduction was associated with antibodies against gametocyte proteins and with recent parasite exposure.

item.title: Nature Communications: Hypothalamic prolactin receptor + dopaminergic neurons regulate energy metabolism and nociceptive threshold in mice during lactation
item.description: The mechanisms by which the brain controls maternal metabolism through hormones remain unclear. Here, authors find PRLR + dopaminergic neurons in the hypothalamus regulate bone and fat metabolism and alter nociceptive threshold through NPY in lactating mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Assessing molecular, cellular and transcriptomic bases of laminar perfusion and cytoarchitecture coupling in the human cortex
item.description: The biological basis of laminar perfusion– cytoarchitecture coupling in the human cortex has remained unclear. Here, the authors introduce CCSI, a non-invasive index linking this coupling to metabolism and functional organization.

item.title: Nature Communications: Commensal bacteria inhibit viral infections via a tryptophan metabolite
item.description: Previous studies suggest that commensal bacteria modulate viral infections. Here, the authors use HIV as a model to show that commensal bacteria impact viral infections, pinpointing a specific tryptophan metabolite as a key player.

item.title: Nature Communications: A microphysiological system HHT-on-a-chip platform recapitulates patient vascular lesions
item.description: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT) is a rare genetic disease involving development of vascular malformations. Here, the authors present the VMO-HHT – an organ-on-a-chip model of HHT that produces vascular malformations like those seen in human HHT patients.

item.title: Nature Communications: The choice-wide behavioral association study: data-driven identification of interpretable behavioral components
item.description: Data-driven methods to discover meaningful differences in complex behavior remain underdeveloped. Here the authors introduce the Choice-Wide Behavioral Association Study, which identifies interpretable behavioral components and reveals previously unrecognized features of behavior across flies, rats, and humans.

item.title: Nature Communications: Engineered polymerase-mediated efficient synthesis of site-specifically functionalized RNA and 2’-modified RNA oligonucleotides via genetic alphabet expansion
item.description: Wu, Mei, Chen and colleagues demonstrate that an engineered XNA polymerase can effectively synthesize the unnatural base pair dNaM-dTPT3 and its analogues, enabling site-specific incorporation of functionalized unnatural base-containing nucleotides into RNA and 2′-modified RNA oligonucleotides.

item.title: Nature Communications: Modulating pressure in the Orbitrap improves sensitivity and mass resolution in charge detection mass spectrometry
item.description: Orbitrap-based single-ion charge mass spectrometry of biomolecular assemblies can be hampered by gas-induced ion losses. Here, the authors introduce a pulsed valve to regulate vacuum conditions resulting in improved ion detection enabling sensitive, accurate, and higher-resolution mass measurements

item.title: Nature Communications: Slow growth as a strategy for plant longevity
item.description: Plant longevity shapes ecosystem functioning and carbon storage, but evidence for its relationship with growth beyond trees has been limited. The authors show that slow growth consistently predicts greater longevity across diverse plant life forms and climatic conditions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Modeling reptile virus infection in vitro using Python regius airway organoids
item.description: Ball python airway organoids, characterized at single-cell resolution, support productive infection with a reptile virus and respond to antiviral drugs, establishing a physiologically relevant model for studying reptile host–pathogen interactions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multi-ancestry genetic architecture of heart failure subtypes
item.description: This study maps the genetic basis of major heart failure subtypes across diverse populations, identifying shared and subtype-specific risk variants that may inform biology, risk prediction and future therapies.

item.title: Nature Communications: AAT/ SERPINA1 Pi*Z variant linked to gestational length and preterm birth prevention via AAT in mice
item.description: Preterm birth affects around 10% of pregnancies and lacks effective preventive therapies. Here, the authors identify the SERPINA1 PiZ variant as a genetic risk factor for shorter gestational duration and show that alpha‑1‑antitrypsin supplementation protects against inflammation‑induced preterm birth in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-wide CRISPR screening identifies cellular factors controlling nonviral genome editing efficiency
item.description: Low editing efficiency of nonviral delivery in post mitotic tissues presents a challenge to the field of gene therapy. Here, authors dissect the genetic regulators of nonviral delivery in post mitotic retinal epithelial cells describe strategies for improved base editor delivery and editing.

item.title: Nature Communications: Phylogenetic reconciliation supports a methanogenic ancestor of the Archaea and a derived origin for host-associated lineages
item.description: Key questions about the early evolution of archaea remain unanswered. Here, Huang et al. use improved methods of genome evolution to propose a euryarchaeal root for archaea, a methanogenic ancestor, and several episodes of genome reduction and expansion, with many symbionts having experienced extensive gene loss.

item.title: Nature Communications: Drops in confidence precede symptoms of obsessive-compulsive disorder
item.description: To devise effective interventions for obsessive-compulsive disorder, it is crucial to understand antecedents to symptom emergence. Here, the authors show evidence for self- and decision making underconfidence preceding symptom escalations.

item.title: Nature Communications: A language network in the individualized functional connectomes of 1199 human brains doing arbitrary tasks
item.description: Shain & Fedorenko examined patterns of correlated activity in the brains of 1,199 people and found that these patterns revealed an integrated brain network selective for language, even when the person was doing something non-linguistic.
